summary.text: Lisa McIntyre is the Democratic candidate for the Michigan House of Representatives, District 22, in the November 3, 2026 general election, in which she faces Republican Casey Noce.
A licensed counselor and member of the Northville Board of Education since 2021, she says her priorities are public schools, affordable health care and mental health support.

paragraphs.text: Lisa McIntyre graduated from R. Nelson Snider High School, earned a bachelor's degree from Kalamazoo College in 1993 and received a graduate degree from the University of Saint Francis in 1997.
In a Ballotpedia survey, she described a career in mental health counseling focused on women, children and families, spanning clinical practice and school and community mental health.
McIntyre has been an at-large member of the Northville Public Schools board since 2021, and her current term ends in 2028.
In the survey, she described herself as the former president and current treasurer of the board and said she is a mother of three.
She said her board work included school safety initiatives and an "away for the day" personal device policy for K-8 students.

Her stated campaign priorities include targeted school funding, better teacher pay, lower prescription drug costs, hospital and insurer price transparency, and incentives to train mental health providers.
